THE POSSIBLE OIL APPEARED DARK/SHIMMERY COMPARED TO SURROUNDING WATER. WINDS NEAR THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE FROM THE SE AT 5-10 KNOTS WHICH ALIGNED WELL WITH THE SLICK'S ORIENTATION. UNCERTAINTIES: UNABLE TO PINPOINT A POSSIBLE POINT SOURCE DUE TO SEVERAL OIL FACILITIES IN THE VICINITY. THE FULL EXTENT OF THE POSSIBLE OIL MAY BE OBSTRUCTED BY PARTIAL CLOUD COVER. IF YOU WOULD LIKE TO SHARE ANY FEEDBACK ABOUT THIS REPORT OR HAVE QUESTIONS, PLEASE CONTACT THE OPERATIONAL ANALYST AT (301) 683-1403 OR SEND TO OCEANMAP@NOAA.GOV. A SUBSURFACE 1 INCH CPVC LINE BETWEEN THE STORAGE TANK AND A WATER RESERVOIR FOREBAY CONTAINING SODIUM HYPOCHLORITE LEAKED INTO THE SURROUNDING SOILS. APPROXIMATELY 500-700 GALLONS OF SODIUM HYPOCHLORITE WAS RELEASED. THE LEAK WAS ESTIMATED TO HAVE BEGAN APPROXIMATELY 2:00 PM WEDNESDAY 6-3-2009, HOWEVER IT WAS NOT DISCOVERED UNTIL 6:30 AM THURSDAY 6-4-2009. A WATER DISTRIBUTION OPERATOR WAS SENT TO INVESTIGATE WHY THE CHLORINE RESIDUAL TO THE RESERVOIR FOREBAY WAS LOST. AT THAT TIME THE OPERATOR THEN DISCOVERED THE LEAK. THE LEAK OCCURRED IN THE LINE WHICH IS BEHIND A RETAINING WALL AND THE SODIUM HYPOCHLORITE WAS SEEPING THROUGH CRACKS IN THE WALL.

A SUBSURFACE 1 INCH CPVC LINE BETWEEN THE STORAGE TANK AND A WATER RESERVOIR FOREBAY CONTAINING SODIUM HYPOCHLORITE LEAKED INTO THE SURROUNDING SOILS. APPROXIMATELY 500-700 GALLONS OF SODIUM HYPOCHLORITE WAS RELEASED. THE LEAK WAS ESTIMATED TO HAVE BEGAN APPROXIMATELY 2:00 PM WEDNESDAY 6-3-2009, HOWEVER IT WAS NOT DISCOVERED UNTIL 6:30 AM THURSDAY 6-4-2009. A WATER DISTRIBUTION OPERATOR WAS SENT TO INVESTIGATE WHY THE CHLORINE RESIDUAL TO THE RESERVOIR FOREBAY WAS LOST. AT THAT TIME THE OPERATOR THEN DISCOVERED THE LEAK. THE LEAK OCCURRED IN THE LINE WHICH IS BEHIND A RETAINING WALL AND THE SODIUM HYPOCHLORITE WAS SEEPING THROUGH CRACKS IN THE WALL.

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 42.220833, -71.767500 (Explicit)
Reported Spill Volume: 5 gallons
Report Description
UP TO 5 GALLONS OF WASTEWATER CONTAINING INCINERATOR ASH RELEASED FROM A VENT TO AN ABOVE GROUND STORAGE TANK CALLED THE "DUMP TANK". THE RELEASE IMPACTED PAVED SURFACES. NO STORM DRAINS, SOIL OR GROUNDWATER WAS IMPACTED. THE TANK IS USED TO STORE CONTACT WATER AND OTHER WASTE WATER CONTAINING ASH PRIOR TO PUMPING THE MATERIAL TO A FILTER PRESS FOR TREATMENT. FACILITY PERSONNEL HAD AIR-PRESSURIZED A LINE TO THE TANK TO REMOVE A BLOCKAGE. THE PRESSURIZATION CAUSED WASTEWATER AND SOLIDS TO OVERFLOW FROM THE TANK'S VENT. THERE IS A POTENTIAL FOR THIS MATERIAL TO BE A RCRA CHARACTERISTIC WASTE AND AS SUCH, THIS RELEASE IS BEING REPORTED AS A PRECAUTION. SUBSEQUENT TESTING OF THE MATERIAL MAY DETERMINE OTHERWISE.

Report Description
///THIS WAS TAKEN FROM A NEWS SOURCE//// CUERO, TEXAS (AP) -- AUTHORITIES SAY NO ONE WAS INJURED AFTER A NATURAL GAS PIPELINE RUPTURE SPARKED A MASSIVE FIRE THAT PROMPTED HOME EVACUATIONS IN SOUTH TEXAS. SPOKESWOMAN WITH THE DEWITT COUNTY EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER SAYS AN ENERGY TRANSFER PARTNERS PIPELINE RUPTURED NEAR LINDENAU, IN A RURAL AREA OF THE COUNTY, AROUND 8 P.M. SUNDAY. SPOKESWOMAN SAID EARLY MONDAY MORNING THAT THE GAS HAD BEEN REROUTED AND THE FIRE WAS OUT. SHE SAYS THERE WERE NO REPORTS OF INJURIES, BUT SEVEN HOMES WERE EVACUATED. RESIDENTS WOULD BE ALLOWED TO RETURN AFTER SAFETY INSPECTIONS WERE COMPLETED. A SPOKESWOMAN FOR TEXAS-BASED ENERGY TRANSFER PARTNERS, SAYS THE COMPANY WILL INVESTIGATE THE CAUSE OF THE RUPTURE. THE VICTORIA ADVOCATE REPORTED THAT THE BLAZE COULD BE SEEN FROM 20 MILES AWAY. LINDENAU IS ABOUT 85 MILES SOUTHEAST OF SAN ANTONIO.

WE ARE A LAND OWNERS IN BARTONVILLE, TX. EIGHT OR MORE NATURAL GAS WELLS SURROUND OUR HOME. OVER THE LAST TWO OR THREE WEEKS A LARGE PART OF OUR PROPERTY HAS FLOODED AND CONTINUES TO FLOOD WITH WHAT WE BELIEVE IS DRAINAGE FROM THE GAS WELL OR WELLS LOCATED NEAR OUR PROPERTY. PARTS OF THE AREA ARE COVERED WITH OILY RESIDUE, THIS RESIDUE IS INCREASING DAILY. THERE IS A PIPELINE ABOUT 10 FEET FROM THE BACK OF MY PROPERTY THAT IS LEAKING AS WELL. WE HAVE PLANTS THAT ARE DYING AND YELLOWING FROM STANDING IN WATER. OUR DOGS HAVE ALSO BEEN SICK OFF AND ON - NOT SURE IF IT IS RELATED, BUT WE'D LIKE TO MAKE THIS NOTED. WE ALSO HAVE THREE PONDS IN OUR NEIGHBORHOOD THAT COULD BE AFFECTED. UPON SMELLING GAS YESTERDAY WE FOLLOWED THE ODOR TO A WELL THAT IS LOCATED APPROXIMATELY 400 YARDS WEST OF OUR PROPERTY. UPON ARRIVING WE DISCOVERED THE WELL WAS RUSTED AND LEAKING A FLUID THAT HAS THE SAME OILY SHEEN AS THE FLUID IN OUR BACKYARD. I WILL TRY AND ATTACH VIDEO AND PHOTOS.

Nearest City: Uniontown, PA

Material: AUTOMOBILE PAINT
Medium Affected: LAND
Suspected Responsible Party: THE CITY OF UNIONTOWN
Skytruth Analysis
AT LEAST 2 LARGE ROLLOFF LOADS OF TOXIC WASTE WAS DUMPED AT A SITE AT THE UNIONTOWN SEWAGE TREATMENT PLANT. THIS MATERIAL WAS FROM AN AUTOMOBILE PARTS STORE LOCATED AT 80 EAST FAYETTE ST IN UNIONTOWN THAT WENT OUT OF BUSINESS. THIS MATERIAL INCLUDED AUTOMOBILE PAINT AND THINNERS, OIL, GREASE, AND EVERYTHING ELSE ONE WOULD FIND IN A PARTS STORE. CITY TRUCKS, ONE DRIVEN BY THE CITIES MAYOR HAULED THIS MATERIAL TO THE TREATMENT PLANT AND DUMPED IT IN THE VERY EARLY HOURS APPROXIMATELY MID SEPTEMBER. THE CITY HAS ALSO BEEN DUMPING REFUSE FROM DEMOLISHED HOUSES IN THE SAME AREA. THESE HOUSES WERE RECENTLY ACQUIRED BY THE CITY FOR A NEW DEVELOPMENT AND WERE PROBABLY NOT CLEARED OF ASBESTOS AND OTHER HAZARDS, THEY WERE DEMOLISHED BY CITY EMPLOYEES. THIS DUMP SITE WAS COVERED WITH BACKFILL, ALSO BEFORE DAYLITE IN THE MORNING. MULCH WAS USED TO COVER THE ODOR OF THE PAINT AND THINNERS.
